reflection.zh: 这则新闻中描述的悲剧性暴力行为提醒我们，使用武力会带来深远的后果。雅伟的话语警告说，那些靠暴力生活的人最终将面临其毁灭性的报应。随着法律程序的展开，我们被提醒杀害人命的严重性以及为此类行为寻求正义的重要性。

title.en: UK a ‘tinderbox’, says Burnham, as he calls in military and bans disposable barbecues – UK politics live
title.zh: 伯纳姆称英国为“火药桶”，呼吁军队协助并禁止一次性烧烤——英国政治直播

summary.en: Officials have described the UK as a “tinderbox” due to extreme heat and fire risk, leading to calls for military assistance and a ban on disposable barbecues. The Prime Minister also announced increased funding for fire and rescue services.
summary.zh: 官员们称英国因极端高温和火灾风险而成为“火药桶”，导致呼吁军队协助并禁止使用一次性烧烤架。首相还宣布增加消防和救援服务的资金。

body.en:
Andy Burnham on Friday announced that has called in the military and temporarily banned on disposable barbecues as wildfires burn in the West Midlands, the Press Association reports.

“Britain is a tinderbox right now, and please just have that in your mind,” he told reporters in Stourbridge as he warned smokers to be careful.

Burnham also said that fire and rescue services will be given more cash to help with their jobs. The prime minister said he will also gather together firefighters for a summit at the end of summer to “make sure they are properly resourced going forwards make sure they are properly resourced going forwards”.

“We’ve lost firefighters in recent years. I know it as a former mayor, from a very grassroots level, some of the pressures on our fire and rescue services. I can’t say today that we’ve done enough to fully resource them to deal with these type of incidents, and I want our firefighters to know that I understand how it seems from their point of view, and I’m going to convene that summit to make sure we get in place the right and support, including the aerial support, permanently if that is what they deem is needed,” Burnham said.
body.zh: 据新闻协会报道，安迪·伯纳姆周五宣布，由于西米德兰兹郡野火燃烧，已召集军队并暂时禁止使用一次性烧烤炉。 “英国现在是一个火药桶，请记住这一点，”他在斯托布里奇告诉记者，同时警告吸烟者要小心。 伯纳姆还表示，消防和救援服务将获得更多现金，以帮助他们开展工作。总理表示，他还将在夏末召集消防队员召开峰会，“确保他们在未来拥有适当的资源”。 “近年来，我们失去了消防员。作为一名前市长，我知道我们的消防和救援服务面临着一些压力。今天我不能说我们已经做了足够的工作来为他们提供充分的资源来处理此类事件，我希望我们的消防员知道我理解他们的观点，我将召开这次峰会，以确保我们永久获得正确的支持和支持，包括空中支持，如果这就是他们认为需要的，”伯纳姆说。

Labour marked its worst performance in more than 50 years when voters went to the polls in Barnsley in May, but 100 days on from those seismic local elections, the political landscape has shifted drastically. Could the South Yorkshire town, where Reform UK reaped the benefits of dissatisfaction with Labour, prove to be a test case for whether the governing party has turned the tide? Continue reading...

title.en: Taliban pressured by insurgents after 5 years in power
title.zh: 塔利班执政五年后受到叛乱分子的压力

summary.en: The Taliban managed to retake power in Afghanistan on August 15, 2021. Now, they face armed factions who challenge the Taliban rule and strain their central claim of providing security.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Taliban managed to retake power in Afghanistan on August 15, 2021. Now, they face armed factions who challenge the Taliban rule and strain their central claim of providing security.

Less than a month before the five-year anniversary of the Taliban retaking power in Afghanistan , the Islamist regime lost control of the Yaftal-e Payeen district capital in the northeastern province of Badakhshan. The disruption was temporary, but it nevertheless marked the first time the Taliban lost control of a district center since returning to power in August 2021 .

Reports from Badakhshan also indicated internal clashes among Taliban fighters and fatal attacks on high-ranking Taliban officials.

On August 2, some two weeks after the brief loss of the district center, former Afghan army general Sami Sadat ordered his forces to launch attacks against the Taliban across the country.

"Today at 5:00 AM, I ordered all military members of the United Front to begin military operations," General Sadat said in a video message released from the US, where he has lived since the fall of Afghanistan to the Taliban.

Other armed groups, including the National Resistance Front led by the son of the late commander Ahmad Shah Massoud, have been engaged in a continuous armed struggle against the Taliban since 2021. While armed insurgents have not been able to pose a major threat to the Taliban's overall grip on power, experts are questioning whether the clashes in Badakhshan could pave the way for more impactful resistance.

"In these five years, this opposition existed in two forms: political and military... As the five-year mark approaches, both forms of opposition have taken shape," former Afghan Interior Minister Mohammad Umer Daudzai told DW.

The Taliban have reigned with an iron fist since the collapse of the US-backed Afghan government five years ago. The Islamist regime denied basic human rights and imposed strict restrictions on women, banning them from work and education beyond the sixth grade. Women are mostly banned from public life in Afghanistan as well, and have few rights at all.

Most former government officials are in exile. While the Taliban maintain that all Afghans are free to return and lead ordinary lives, opponents counter that return is only viable if political activity is permitted.

While the regime managed to cultivate some contacts internationally , they are still viewed as illegitimate by most of the world's governments. To date, only Russia has acknowledged the Taliban as the official government of Afghanistan.

body.zh: 塔利班于 2021 年 8 月 15 日成功在阿富汗重新掌权。现在，他们面临着挑战塔利班统治并对其提供安全这一核心主张施加压力的武装派别。 距离塔利班在阿富汗重新掌权五周年不到一个月，伊斯兰政权失去了对东北部巴达赫尚省亚夫塔尔帕延地区首府的控制。这次破坏是暂时的，但这仍然标志着塔利班自 2021 年 8 月重新掌权以来首次失去对地区中心的控制。 来自巴达赫尚省的报道还表明，塔利班武装分子之间发生了内部冲突，塔利班高级官员遭到致命袭击。 8 月 2 日，在短暂失去地区中心大约两周后，前阿富汗陆军将军萨米·萨达特命令他的部队向全国各地的塔利班发动袭击。 萨达特将军在美国发布的视频信息中说：“今天凌晨 5:00，我命令统一战线的所有军事人员开始军事行动。” 自阿富汗落入塔利班手中以来，萨达特将军一直居住在美国。 其他武装团体，包括已故指挥官艾哈迈德·沙阿·马苏德之子领导的民族抵抗阵线，自2021年以来一直在与塔利班进行持续的武装斗争。虽然武装叛乱分子未能对塔利班的总体权力构成重大威胁，但专家们质疑巴达赫尚省的冲突是否能为更有影响力的抵抗铺平道路。 阿富汗前内政部长穆罕默德·乌梅尔·道扎伊告诉德国之声：“在这五年里，这种反对派以两种形式存在：政治和军事……随着五年的临近，两种形式的反对派都已形成。” 自五年前美国支持的阿富汗政府垮台以来，塔利班一直实行铁腕统治。伊斯兰政权剥夺基本人权，并对妇女施加严格限制，禁止她们工作和接受六年级以上的教育。在阿富汗，妇女也大多被禁止参与公共生活，几乎没有任何权利。 大多数前政府官员都在流亡。虽然塔利班坚称所有阿富汗人都可以自由返回并过上正常生活，但反对者反驳说，只有在允许政治活动的情况下，返回才是可行的。 尽管该政权设法在国际上建立了一些联系，但世界上大多数政府仍认为这些联系是非法的。迄今为止，只有俄罗斯承认塔利班是阿富汗的官方政府。 面对国内外压力，塔利班多次将恢复国家安全作为其合法性的首要诉求。然而，专家警告说，他们的治理风格可能会......

title.en: Congo: Ebola cases are rising at record pace
title.zh: 刚果：埃博拉病例以创纪录速度增长

summary.en: The Ebola virus is rapidly spreading in the Democratic Republic of Congo, leading to growing fears of a severe health crisis in the densely populated city of Kinshasa. Hospitals are urgently working to prepare for the escalating emergency.
summary.zh: 埃博拉病毒正在刚果民主共和国迅速蔓延。在拥有数百万人口的城市金沙萨，人们对一场严重的健康危机日益感到担忧。各医院正在尽力为紧急情况做准备。

body.en:
The Ebola virus is spreading rapidly in the DRC. In Kinshasa, a city of millions, fears of a serious health crisis are growing. Hospitals are scrambling to prepare for emergencies as best as they can.

The Ebola  epidemic in the eastern part of the  Democratic Republic of the Congo has now spread to a sixth province in the country. Concerns are growing that the life-threatening infectious disease could spread to the capital, Kinshasa, which is home to 19 million people.

Facilities for isolating patients are ready for the event that a public health alert should reach the capital, says Jean-Jacques Muyembe, Director General of the National Institute for Biomedical Research (INRB).

"If there is a suspected case, the epidemiological services and the INRB laboratory are ready to quickly identify and confirm cases," he told DW.

The Ministry of Health has set up the Cinquantenaire Hospital so that it can admit and fully isolate patients if necessary. We are prepared. We can quickly contain an Ebola outbreak here in Kinshasa."

However, the virus has been spreading faster than health authorities can contain it. This Ebola outbreak is driven by the rare Bundiyugyo strain of the virus, for which no vaccine or treatment has yet been approved.

According to Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus , Director-General of the World Health Organization (WHO), the outbreak, given its rapid rise, could surpass the West African Ebola outbreak of 2014 – 2016. .

At that time, 11,000 people died, while the current health crisis has already claimed 2,000 lives, with more than 4,300 cases recorded to date. Authorities officially announced the outbreak on May 15; three months later, the country remains on edge.

The WHO meanwhile expects the current outbreak to only  peak in six months .

The initial infections meanwhile can be traced back to as early as February, according to reports. The epicenter of the outbreak was identified as the northeastern province of Ituri, which has been plagued by insecurity for years, and is home a large number of internally displaced persons.

Many other cases have meanwhile also been reported in the provinces of North and South Kivu, where the security situation is even a bigger problem; authorities have effectively lost control over entire areas in their years-long conflict with M23 rebels and affiliated groups.

Fear among the population of contracting the virus is also growing every day. A week ago, the threat came close to the capital when a boat was stopped at the port of Maluku, about 65 kilometers upstream from Kinshasa.

title.en: Builders unearth €9m gold stash sealed in walls of Belgian property
title.zh: 建筑工人在比利时房产墙壁中挖出900万欧元黄金

summary.en: Construction workers in Belgium unearthed a stash of €9 million in gold while drilling to install sewage pipes in a cellar wall.
summary.zh: 比利时建筑工人在钻孔铺设污水管道时，在地下室墙壁中挖出了价值900万欧元的黄金。

body.en:
Builders renovating a house in Belgium have discovered a stash of gold reportedly worth some €9m (£7.6m) sealed into the walls of its cellar.

The construction workers stumbled across the hidden trove of gold bars and coins while drilling to lay new sewage pipes in the property in east Flanders earlier this week, local media report.

The discovery has sparked interest in who might get to keep the hoard - with both the builders and the local charity that owns the site having a chance of claiming it.

After launching an investigation, police warned people against attending the site to search for more treasure, saying the house was "turned upside down" and all the gold had been moved to a secure location.

The builders - including an 18-year-old working a summer job - unearthed the stash while working on the building's foundations.

"Our first reaction was actually disbelief, amazement," the student, named Kobe, told Belgian public broadcaster VRT.

"At first I thought they were €1 coins. But then we also saw a gold nugget lying there. That's when we realised it was something bigger."

Soon after, they alerted police to the discovery and explained that keeping it for themselves was not an option.

"There are so many coins and bars - it would be almost impossible," the site manager Mario told VRT.

The property currently belongs to CAW Oost-Vlaanderen, which provides welfare support in Dendermonde, a Flemish community of around 47,000 people.

Its director, Geert Hillaert, said his first reaction was "surprise and amazement", adding that he hoped the treasure might eventually be used to support the charity's work and meet the "enormous need we experience daily".

Local police urged the public not to visit the active construction site looking for treasure.

The force - which has updated its Facebook profile picture to an image of a gold coin - said it hoped the discovery would end up in "the right place" and change people's lives.

The rightful owner has five years to claim the hoard under Belgian law - though the local prosecutor, who has launched an investigation, said it was not yet known who this might be.

If no one comes forward, civil law states that hidden treasure on someone else's property be divided between the finder and the property's owner.

This only applies, though, if the stash is not found to be linked to criminal activity.

Both the builders and the charity now face a wait of up to 1,823 days for an owner to come forward. If no one speaks up to successfully claim it, silence truly will be golden.
body.zh: 比利时翻修一所房屋的建筑商在其地窖的墙壁上发现了据报道价值约 900 万欧元（760 万英镑）的黄金藏品。 据当地媒体报道，本周早些时候，建筑工人在东佛兰德斯的一处房产中钻孔铺设新的污水管道时，偶然发现了隐藏的金条和金币宝藏。 这一发现引发了人们对谁可以保留这些战利品的兴趣——建筑商和拥有该遗址的当地慈善机构都有机会认领这些战利品。 调查已经展开，当地警方警告任何希望寻找更多宝藏的人，该地点已被“颠倒”，黄金已转移到安全地点。 建筑商在打地基时挖出了这些宝藏，其中包括一名正在做暑期工的 18 岁年轻人。 “我们的第一反应实际上是难以置信、惊讶，”这位名叫科比的学生告诉比利时公共广播公司 VRT。 “一开始我以为它们是 1 欧元的硬币。但后来我们还看到了一块金块躺在那里。那时我们才意识到它是更大的东西。” 不久之后，他们向警方通报了这一发现，并解释说他们不能自己保留它。 “有这么多的金币和金条——这几乎是不可能的，”网站经理马里奥告诉 VRT。 该房产目前属于 CAW Oost-Vlaanderen，该公司为登德尔蒙德提供福利支持，登德尔蒙德是一个拥有约 47,000 人的佛兰德斯社区。 其负责人基尔特·希拉特 (Geert Hillaert) 表示，他的第一反应是“惊讶和惊讶”，并补充说，他希望这些战利品最终可以用来支持该慈善机构的工作，并满足“我们每天经历的巨大需求”。 当地警方敦促公众不要前往正在施工的建筑工地寻找宝藏。 该部队已将其 Facebook 个人资料图片更新为金币图片，并表示希望这一发现最终出现在“正确的地方”并改变人们的生活。 根据比利时法律，合法所有者有五年时间索取这些宝藏，不过已展开调查的当地检察官表示，目前尚不清楚该人是谁。 如果没有人挺身而出，民法规定，隐藏在他人财产中的宝藏将由发现者和财产所有者分配。 不过，这只适用于未发现赃物与犯罪活动有关的情况。 现在，建筑商和慈善机构都需要等待长达 1,823 天才能找到业主。如果没人发声才能成功夺取，沉默才是金。

reflection.en: The discovery of hidden gold reminds us that earthly treasures, however valuable, are ultimately transient. Yahweh invites us to invest in what truly lasts, building up treasures in heaven that cannot be stolen or decay.
reflection.zh: 发现隐藏的黄金提醒我们，地上的财宝，无论多么珍贵，最终都是短暂的。雅伟邀请我们投资于真正永恒的事物，在天上积攒那不能被盗或朽坏的财宝。

verse.textEn: Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moths and vermin destroy.
verse.textZh: 不要为自己积攒财宝在地上；地上有虫子咬，能锈坏。

title.en: Can a giant Madonna help slow secularization in Poland?
title.zh: 巨型麦当娜能否帮助减缓波兰的世俗化？

summary.en: Europe's largest statue of the Virgin Mary will be inaugurated on Saturday in the Polish village of Konotopie. What will the monument mean for the village it towers over and for the Catholic faith in Poland in general?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及在压力下的忠信与属灵勇气。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Europe's largest statue of the Virgin Mary will be inaugurated on Saturday in the Polish village of Konotopie. What will the monument mean for the village it towers over and for the Catholic faith in Poland in general?

With its grain fields, meadows and lake, the countryside around the tiny village of Konotopie in central Poland is idyllic. Now there is a monumental statue of the Virgin Mary towering above all this.

Home to just 120 residents and situated about 160 kilometers (99 miles) northwest of the capital, Warsaw, the previously little-known village of Konotopie has been in the headlines for weeks now as a result of the massive statue.

The snow-white structure, which is visible for miles around, is more than 55 meters (180 feet) tall. The statue itself is 40.6 meters high and stands on a 15-meter-high pedestal shaped like a crown that is intended to serve as a viewing platform.

The figure dwarfs Rio de Janeiro's famous statue of Christ the Redeemer, which reaches a total height of 38 meters including its base.

The statue will be officially inaugurated on Saturday, August 15, the feast of the Assumption of Mary, a major holy day in the Catholic calendar.

Although final construction work is still underway and the site remains fenced off and guarded, thousands of people — both pilgrims and sightseers — have been flocking to see it for months.

"It's a nightmare," one critic of the statue told the weekly magazine Newsweek, "a complete waste. Instead of investing that money in useful projects, they financed a giant pile of concrete."

"This Mary is absolutely beautiful. My utmost respect. A fantastic achievement," said one devout woman visiting the site, according to the right-wing conservative weekly Sieci .

The benefactor behind the statue, 75-year-old Roman Karkosik, hails from a nearby village and is one of Poland's wealthiest individuals.

Nearly 40 years ago, when the shortage economy of socialism gave way to free-market capitalism after the collapse of communism in eastern Europe, Karkosik was a young graduate from technical high school.

He started out as a bartender, but moved on to buying and selling scrap metal, producing soft drinks and later became the first entrepreneur in Poland to manufacture plastic bottles.

Karkosik made a name for himself on the Warsaw Stock Exchange. Some journalists have compared his role in Poland to Warren Buffett's influence on Wall Street.

His fortune is estimated at roughly €442 million ($511 million), and he ranks 44th on Wprost magazine's list of Poland's richest people. He lives in an 18th-century manor in the town of Kikol, just two kilometers from Konotopie.

Karkosik and his wife, Grazyna, avoid both public appearances and contact with the media.

title.en: Instagram accounts fuelling Ceuta crisis with paid advice for help to cross
title.zh: Instagram 账户通过付费建议帮助穿越，加剧了休达危机

summary.en: BBC's Top Comment podcast has found a network of Instagram profiles glamourising the swim around the Morocco-Ceuta border fence.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
This weekend, Mohammed wants to travel from Morocco to the neighbouring Spanish enclave of Ceuta, on the northern tip of Africa.

He's a Moroccan man in his twenties and wants to emigrate to Europe - not least because he's been seeing lots of videos on Instagram that make the trip look easy.

He contacts several of the Instagram accounts and one replies, claiming to have helped "many people" and offering him advice on how to cross for hundreds of pounds.

Except Mohammed isn't real - he's a dummy account I've set up to investigate a network of interconnected Instagram profiles that are driving the influx of migrants to Ceuta with aspirational content and offering them help for a fee.

It comes after roughly 78,000 migrants from Morocco arrived by sea into Ceuta in a matter of hours last month, 100 of whom died according to the Mayor of Ceuta.

The crisis has calmed since, but it has sparked tensions between EU nations who share open borders as well as criticism of the Spanish government.

The BBC's Top Comment podcast has identified dozens of Instagram profiles that portray the short swim around the Morocco-Ceuta border fence as safe and easy - but in reality, people have drowned trying to make the crossing and take much longer routes. The accounts also wrongly show Ceuta as a viable route to mainland Europe.

Our research suggests that this has contributed to the influx, alongside other factors such as misinformation about changes to Spanish immigration law and allegations about weak border controls.

After engaging with the accounts' profiles and posts, the BBC was added to multiple channels and WhatsApp groups. When I asked one of the anonymous accounts if they could help me cross to Ceuta this weekend, they said yes and requested "5000 dirhams upfront" (£400) for "information that will help you enter Ceuta".

They said they had helped "many people" cross before and would give me information about the "sewer pipes" which I could use to help me reach the enclave safely.

The account confirmed lots of other Instagram profiles help people to cross to Ceuta in this way, and asked for payment "via bank account" with a specific money transfer service.

But they didn't respond when asked whether I would get a refund if the crossing was not successful. They've since deleted several of their messages to the account.

The same profile giving this advice had previously told my real, BBC Instagram account that "it does not encourage immigration to Ceuta" - a message several other profiles repeated.

And it's continuing - social media posts, actively recommended by Instagram's algorithm, are advertising another attempt at the crossing this weekend. This risks further deaths and inflamed diplomatic tensions between Morocco and Spain.

title.en: Presidential vote counting halted in Zambia over alleged attacks on polling staff
title.zh: 赞比亚因涉嫌袭击投票站工作人员而暂停总统计票

summary.en: The electoral commission said violence had "resulted in the theft of marked ballot papers".
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Zambia's electoral commission has suspended the counting of votes from Thursday's presidential, parliamentary and local elections over alleged attacks on polling staff.

The authority said the process would be halted nationwide with immediate effect as it expressed concern over reports of violence that had "resulted in the theft of marked ballot papers in ballot boxes".

President Hakainde Hichilema is seeking a second five-year term. Brian Mundubile is the main opposition candidate among 13 challengers.

The electoral commission had previously set itself the target of announcing the results by the end of Sunday.

Counting got under way immediately after polls closed on Thursday but no official results had been declared when the halt in the count came into effect.

In Friday's statement the commission said it would review the decision to suspend vote counting within the next 24 hours.

Just hours before the commission's statement, Mundubile expressed "grave concern" over delays in the announcement of presidential results, warning that the delay could create opportunities for interference or manipulation.

He cited what he described as "deeply troubling reports" from several areas, including alleged military involvement at totalling centres and allegations concerning the movement of ballot boxes.

He called for the immediate publication of results polling station by polling station, protection of the chain of custody and investigations into the reported incidents.

Hichilema also issued a statement urging Zambians to "remain peaceful, patient and patriotic as we await the official outcome from those entrusted with managing the vote".

Polling day was largely peaceful, with queues reported in many areas and only isolated delays. Along with electing a president and MPs, the more than eight million registered voters had the chance to choose a new parliament and local councils.

Thursday's vote was seen as a test of Zambia's reputation as one of Africa's most stable democracies, amid concerns that political freedoms are being undermined.

Despite 14 candidates being on the presidential ballot paper, the contest was largely seen as a two-horse race between the incumbent and his main challenger Mundubile - running on the banner of the National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP).

Hichilema is credited with steering Zambia through a difficult economic climate but his popularity was dented as many people said their circumstances have not improved. Mundubile hoped to capitalise on that dissatisfaction.

title.en: The major citizenship ruling affecting Australians like Ophelia

body.en:
When Ophelia Bryant first travelled to Italy in 1986, she says she felt something she could not quite explain.

Her parents had been born in Italy, as had all four of her grandparents. They immigrated to Australia in 1955, where Bryant was born three years later.

Italy has remained a constant in her life, with Bryant returning more than a dozen times to visit relatives and reconnect with her family roots.

But when she began looking into whether she could formally claim Italian citizenship, she discovered her family history came with a legal complication.

Her parents became Australian citizens in 1961, when Bryant was a child, and later formally renounced their Italian citizenship.

Under a restrictive interpretation of Italy's citizenship laws, known as the 'minor issue', that could break the line of citizenship transmission.

Now, a landmark decision by Italy's highest court has changed that legal interpretation — and Bryant is "optimistic because that door may finally be open".

The so-called minor issue arose from conflicting interpretations of Italy's 1912 citizenship law.

One provision established that children born overseas to an Italian citizen could acquire Italian citizenship from birth.

Another was interpreted as meaning that when an Italian parent became a citizen of another country, their minor children could lose their Italian citizenship along with them.

That interpretation gained ground through Italian court decisions from 2023 onwards, leading to the rejection of citizenship-by-descent applications.

But in July, Italy's Supreme Court's United Sections, the court's highest panel for resolving conflicting legal interpretations, ruled that citizenship acquired at birth was not automatically lost when an Italian parent subsequently naturalised in another country.

Brisbane-based Italian lawyer Fabrizio Fiorino, who advises clients on Italian citizenship applications, said the decision effectively restores the previous interpretation of the law.

"It was not a change in a provision, but it was a change in the interpretation of rules," he said.

He told SBS News the ruling means people who were Italian citizens from birth cannot simply be considered to have lost that citizenship because their parents later became foreign citizens while they were minors.

For thousands of people whose citizenship applications were rejected on that basis, the decision could provide a pathway back.

Italy's interior ministry has since issued a letter instructing authorities to follow the Supreme Court's interpretation.

body.en:
Record ‌rainfall has left thousands of travellers stranded at Tokyo's Narita airport as ‌flooding disrupted transport, knocked out power and claimed at least four lives.

More than 360mm of rain fell in the 24 hours to Friday in parts of Chiba prefecture, which adjoins the capital ‌Tokyo, inundating roads ‌and railways. The heavy rain caused power outages to nearly 25,000 households during one of Japan's busiest holiday weeks.

Authorities said four deaths have been confirmed, including at least one person who had been trapped in a submerged vehicle.

"This case ⁠was an extremely unusual situation, even ‌by Japan's historical weather standards," Chiba governor Toshihito Kumagai told reporters on Friday.

Major highways in Chiba, including routes linking Narita airport, one of Japan's main international transport hubs, with central Tokyo, remained closed, forcing drivers onto alternative routes and causing heavy traffic, according to highway operator NEXCO East.

Several rail services remained suspended on Friday morning, though some trains connecting Narita ⁠to Tokyo had resumed operations.

Elsewhere in the Pacific, Hawaii has declared a state of emergency on Friday as it prepared for Tropical Storm Lala, which could bring powerful winds, flooding and landslides this weekend.

The Pacific storm is gaining strength according to the United States' National Weather Service, which expects it to become a hurricane as it approaches.

Winds were blowing at around 80km/h and the storm could dump up to 63.5 cm of rain in parts of the Hawaii, the weather service added.

Governor Josh Green declared a state of emergency in response to the threat, an administrative measure that frees up funds, resources and personnel in the event of damage.

"Tropical Storm Lala poses a serious threat to our state, particularly Hawaii Island — and we are taking action now to ensure resources are available where they are needed," he said.

The United States says it could maintain a naval blockade of Iran indefinitely and would ratchet up economic pressure on the country as ceasefire talks floundered.

Amid the stalemate, global oil supply has continued to drop while regional tensions have risen.

Iran has imposed an effective blockade of the strait since the US and Israel initiated attacks in late February, and wants to charge tolls for passage. Continued attacks in the strait, which had been free to transit before the war, led to the collapse of an April ceasefire and the breach of a  memorandum of understanding signed in June .

US defence secretary Pete Hegseth told reporters that the US military has the capability to maintain a naval presence in the region to enforce its blockade of Iran, which has inflicted severe economic damage on the country.

"Indefinitely, the United States Navy can maintain a blockade like that because we'll rotate ships in and out, as we have, and we'll continue to," Hegseth told reporters during a trip to Panama.

With a tentative June deal to end the war in tatters, Iran has sought to exert leverage on the US in return by controlling the Strait of Hormuz.

It has attacked some vessels trying to transit the strategic waterway, through which a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas travelled before the war began in February.

Two vessels from the state-owned Abu Dhabi National Oil Company were attacked transiting the strait on Friday, UAE state news agency WAM reported. The United Arab Emirates government condemned it as an Iranian attack.

US President Donald Trump is under pressure at home to end a war that is deeply unpopular, with high fuel prices dragging down his approval ratings and potentially eroding his party's control of congress in midterm elections in November.

Trump has repeatedly said the US has "total control" over the strait, prompting Iranian denials. Iran has said it would not allow the waterway to reopen until its conditions are met . These include removing economic sanctions and releasing frozen Iranian assets.

summary.en: Romania has shut down its sole nuclear power plant due to insufficient cooling water from the Danube River. Meanwhile, Hungary is working to construct a dam on the Danube to maintain operations at its Paks nuclear facility.
summary.zh: 罗马尼亚因多瑙河冷却水不足而关闭了其唯一的核电站。与此同时，匈牙利正加紧在多瑙河上修建水坝，以维持其帕克斯核电站的运行。

body.zh: 由于多瑙河缺乏冷却水，罗马尼亚关闭了其唯一的核电站，这是一项罕见的举措。与此同时，匈牙利正在竞相在多瑙河上筑坝，试图保持其帕克斯核电站的正常运行。 罗马尼亚周四关闭了其唯一的核电站，这是在干旱导致多瑙河和欧洲其他主要水道水位创历史新低的情况下采取的罕见举措。 多瑙河是切尔纳沃达电厂的唯一冷却水源，该电厂通常发电量约占罗马尼亚电力的五分之一。 该电站此前仅在 2023 年因干旱和炎热的夏季而关闭过一次。 与此同时，匈牙利正忙着在多瑙河上筑坝，试图使其帕克斯核电站至少保持在最近几天维持的最低水平，远低于其容量。 罗马尼亚核电公司上个月已经关闭了切尔纳沃达的两座反应堆之一。 周四，该公司表示，“由于多瑙河水位持续大幅下降”，需要关闭第二个。 本月早些时候，该公司在海军的帮助下尝试提高工厂保持运营的机会。 最令人难忘的是，它炸毁了因低水位而暴露的岩石露头，并战略性地将岩石沉积在河床上，以将更多的水引导到切尔纳沃达。 但最终，持续的干燥天气和水位下降导致了全面关闭。 工厂厂长罗密欧·乌尔詹 (Romeo Urjan) 告诉法新社：“我们预计未来 10 天内不会重新启动。” 罗马尼亚能源部表示，正在采购替代能源，包括风电和进口能源，以确保充足的供应。尽管如此，它仍然呼吁公众负责任地消费。 它警告说，作为最后的手段，大型工业用户将不得不在晚上面临限制以节省电力。汽车制造商福特和达契亚已承诺暂停生产至 8 月 19 日，以节省电力。 周四，彼得·马扎尔总理参观了匈牙利唯一的核电站——帕克斯核电站，该电站也由多瑙河冷却。 马扎尔在布达佩斯以南约 100 公里（约 60 英里）的现场告诉记者：“我们已经开始建造低堰，这将永久有助于提高多瑙河的水位。” 九天前，该工厂面临完全关闭的风险，但政府在最后一刻中止了这些计划，因为多瑙河的水位最终比预测高了几毫米。 正常情况下，该工厂负责匈牙利约一半的...

reflection.en: The drying Danube River, forcing nations to adapt their energy strategies, reminds us of humanity's ancient charge to care for creation. Yahweh placed us in the garden to work and keep it, a responsibility that calls for wisdom and foresight in managing our shared natural resources. This situation highlights the delicate balance between human needs and the...
reflection.zh: 多瑙河的干涸迫使各国调整能源策略，这提醒我们人类肩负着看护受造物的古老使命。雅伟将我们安置在园中，要我们耕作和看守，这项责任要求我们在管理共享自然资源时，具备智慧和远见。这一局面突显了人类需求与维持我们生存的生态系统健康之间的微妙平衡。

verse.textEn: Yahweh God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and take care of it.
verse.textZh: 雅伟神将那人安置在伊甸园，使他修理看守。

title.en: China Desk
title.zh: 中国观察

strap.en: Policy signals, social change, and national developments inside China.
strap.zh: 聚焦中国内部政策走向、社会变化与国家动态。

title.en: US says dozens of countries helped China dodge Trump's tariffs
title.zh: 美国称数十个国家帮助中国规避特朗普关税

summary.en: A new US report indicates that China utilized various countries with lower tariffs to reroute goods, thereby avoiding higher levies imposed by the Trump administration.
summary.zh: 一份新的美国报告指出，中国通过关税较低的国家转运货物，以规避特朗普政府征收的更高关税。

body.en:
The White House said in a report on Thursday that more than 40 countries had helped China sidestep US tariffs by routing exports through nations that face lower American import duties.

The countries named include Canada, India, Mexico, Japan and South Korea, which the White House said had helped China evade tens of billions of dollars in tariffs, which are levied on companies importing goods.

White House trade adviser Peter Navarro said it had cost "American jobs and billions in revenue".

A spokesperson for the Chinese embassy in Washington said "trade wars have no winners" and that it opposes the US tariff measures and the use of state power to target China's companies.

"Any unilateral actions or agreements concerning transshipped goods must not target or harm the interests of third parties," the spokesperson added.

The BBC has contacted the US embassies of Canada, India, Mexico, Japan, South Korea and other trading partners listed in the report for comment.

The report follows a wave of sanctions between the US and China and comes weeks before US President Donald Trump will meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Washington.

Between $30bn (£22bn) and roughly $300bn in goods have been moved from countries with higher tariffs through those with lower rates, according to government and private sector estimates quoted by the White House.

The process is known as transshipping, which refers to the practice of transferring cargo through another country while en route to a final destination.

The US accused China of "taking advantage" of the practice by moving goods through nations that have lower import duties.

China has used third countries as a stopover and has repackaged goods to hide their real origin to obtain lower tariffs, the White House said in its report, describing the process as "fraud cloaked in paperwork".

"What has changed in today's Great Transshipment Scam is not merely the speed and scale of this modern form of smuggling, but the breadth, depth, and sophistication of the global Shadow Transshipment Network through which China's tariff evasion now moves," the White House wrote.

The US has deployed artificial intelligence tools to catch transshipment efforts, it added.

The report is expected to add to key sticking points between the sides as Trump and Xi prepare to meet in the US in September, and Chang Pao Li, associate professor of economics at Singapore Management University, said it could be used to strengthen the US bargaining position.

"Washington can argue that China has preserved access to the US market indirectly and that any broader trade settlement must therefore address not only direct Chinese exports but also third-country routing," she told the BBC.

Chang said while changes in trade-flow patterns may partly reflect...
body.zh: 白宫周四在一份报告中表示，已有 40 多个国家通过美国进口关税较低的国家进行出口，帮助中国规避美国关税。 被点名的国家包括加拿大、印度、墨西哥、日本和韩国，白宫称这些国家帮助中国逃避了数百亿美元的关税。 白宫贸易顾问彼得·纳瓦罗表示，这损失了“美国的就业机会和数十亿美元的收入”。 中国驻华盛顿大使馆发言人在回应BBC询问时表示，“贸易战没有赢家”，反对美国采取关税措施，反对动用国家力量针对中国企业。 该发言人补充说，“任何涉及转运货物的单方面行动或协议均不得针对或损害第三方利益。” BBC已联系加拿大、印度、墨西哥、日本、韩国和报告中列出的其他贸易伙伴的美国大使馆征求评论。 该报告是在美国和中国之间实施一波制裁之后发布的，几周前唐纳德·特朗普总统将在华盛顿会见中国领导人习近平。 根据白宫引用的政府和私营部门的估计，价值 300 亿美元（222 亿英镑）至约 3000 亿美元的商品已从关税较高的国家转移到关税较低的国家。 这一过程被称为转运，是指在前往最终目的地的途中通过另一个国家转运货物的做法。 美国指责中国“利用”这种做法，通过关税较低的国家运送货物。 白宫在报告中表示，中国利用第三国作为中转站，并对货物进行重新包装以隐藏其真实来源，以获得较低的关税，并将这一过程描述为“披着文书外衣的欺诈行为”。 白宫写道：“今天的大转运骗局所改变的不仅仅是这种现代走私形式的速度和规模，还有中国逃税活动所通过的全球影子转运网络的广度、深度和复杂性。” 它补充说，美国已部署人工智能（AI）工具来追踪转运工作。 随着特朗普和习近平准备九月在美国会面，这份报告预计将加剧双方之间的关键症结。 尽管在 2025 年 5 月谈判后暂停了大部分关税，但华盛顿和北京仍在继续相互制裁，包括限制运往美国的人形机器人以及中国收紧对无人机出口的限制。 2025 年 4 月，特朗普宣布对数十个美国贸易伙伴征收全面关税，因为他长期以来相信关税将有助于促进美国就业和经济增长。 这些制裁后来被美国最高法院取消......

reflection.en: The practice of rerouting goods to avoid tariffs raises questions about integrity and fair dealing in international commerce. Yahweh delights in honest measures and transparent transactions, reminding us that ethical conduct is paramount in all economic activities. This principle calls for fairness and truthfulness, even when navigating complex trade...
reflection.zh: 通过转运货物来规避关税的做法，引发了关于国际贸易诚信和公平交易的疑问。雅伟喜悦诚实的度量和透明的交易，提醒我们在所有经济活动中，道德行为至关重要。这一原则呼吁我们在处理复杂的贸易法规时，也要秉持公平和真实。

verse.textEn: Yahweh detests dishonest scales, but accurate weights find favor with him.
verse.textZh: 诡诈的天平为雅伟所憎恶；公平的法码为他所喜悦。

title.en: ‘Tiktok wouldn’t open at all’: Taiwan simulates an internet blackout, with an eye on China threat
title.zh: “抖音完全打不开”：台湾模拟互联网中断，以应对中国威胁

summary.en: Taiwan conducted its first internet blackout simulation, prompted by concerns over the security of its undersea cables, which are vital for its digital connectivity. During the exercise in Taipei, air raid sirens sounded, mobile alerts pinged, and police directed people off the streets.
summary.zh: 台湾周四首次进行互联网中断模拟演习，原因是担心作为其“数字生命线”的海底电缆的安全。在台北的演习中，防空警报响起，手机警报提示音不断，警察引导人们离开街道。

body.en: Taiwan practised cutting off internet for the first time amid concerns about the safety of the undersea cables that form its ‘digital lifeline’ In Taipei, the streets swiftly empty as air raid sirens ring out and alerts ping on mobile phones. Police officers usher any stragglers into shelters, leaving the capital suddenly deserted. In cities across Taiwan, these kinds of drills are a fact of life every year , amid the growing threat posed by China across the strait, but this time there is something different. Continue reading...
body.zh: 由于担心构成其“数字生命线”的海底电缆的安全性，台湾周四首次练习切断互联网。在台北，随着空袭警报的响起和手机上的警报声，街道迅速空无一人。警察把掉队的人带进避难所，首都突然变得空无一人。在台湾各城市，随着海峡两岸中国构成的威胁日益加剧，此类演习每年都是家常便饭，但这次有所不同。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Taiwan's simulation of an internet blackout highlights the deep anxieties nations face regarding critical infrastructure and potential threats. In moments of such vulnerability and preparation, the ancient promise of Yahweh reminds us not to fear or be dismayed, for divine presence offers strength and help. This spiritual anchor can guide communities as...
reflection.zh: 台湾模拟互联网中断，凸显了各国在关键基础设施和潜在威胁面前的深层焦虑。在面对这种脆弱和准备的时刻，雅伟的古老应许提醒我们不要惧怕，也不要惊惶，因为神圣的同在提供力量和帮助。这个属灵的锚点可以指引社群应对复杂的挑战并建立韧性。

verse.textEn: So do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God.
verse.textZh: 你不要害怕，因为我与你同在；不要惊惶，因为我是你的神。

title.en: The west turns a blind eye to Xi Jinping’s repressive regime in China | Letters
title.zh: 西方国家对习近平在中国的压制性政权视而不见 | 来信

summary.en: Jennifer Hubbard and other letter writers express concern that Western nations are ignoring China's repressive regime, particularly its 'ethnic unity' law used to suppress minorities. They argue that meaningful international diplomacy is urgently needed to address these human rights issues.
summary.zh: 詹妮弗·哈伯德及其他来信者表示，西方国家对中国压制性政权，特别是其用于压制少数民族的“民族团结”法视而不见。他们认为，急需有意义的国际外交来解决这些人权问题。

body.en: Meaningful diplomacy on an international level is well overdue, writes Jennifer Hubbard . Plus letters from Geoffrey Dixon and Jane Renton In his article on China’s latest tool for suppression of minorities, the “ethnic unity” law, Simon Tisdall seems to take it as read that western governments will continue to pay lip service to notions of human rights in China while pursuing short-term economic goals, ultimately destructive to their own productivity ( President Xi never wastes a good crisis. As Iran, Ukraine and Palestine distract the world, he tightens his grip, 8 August ). This has been the pattern since June 1989, the Tiananmen Square massacre. His faint hope that the young urban Chinese might overturn Xi’s regime is a judgment on the failure of western governments to show any foresight, integrity, effective diplomacy, joined-up thinking or action. They rely on the self-sacrifice of individuals such as Jimmy Lai , Lobga Rangzen and countless – often to us nameless – individuals who put their lives on the line while we wring our hands and weep crocodile tears. Continue reading...
body.zh: 詹妮弗·哈伯德写道，早就应该在国际层面开展有意义的外交。再加上杰弗里·迪克森和简·伦顿的来信。西蒙·蒂斯达尔在其关于中国镇压少数民族的最新工具“民族团结”法的文章中似乎认为，西方政府将继续对中国的人权观念口头上说好，同时追求短期经济目标，最终损害他们自己的生产力（习主席从来不会浪费一场好的危机。随着伊朗、乌克兰和巴勒斯坦分散了世界的注意力，他加强了控制，8月8日）。这就是1989年6月天安门广场屠杀以来的模式。他对中国城市年轻人可能推翻习近平政权的微弱希望是对西方政府未能表现出任何远见、正直、有效外交、联合思维或行动的判断。他们依赖于黎智英（Jimmy Lai）、洛布加·让赞（Lobga Rangzen）等个人的自我牺牲，以及无数（通常对我们来说无名）个人的自我牺牲，他们冒着生命危险，而我们则绞尽脑汁，流下鳄鱼的眼泪。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The call for international diplomacy to address the suppression of minorities echoes the biblical mandate to speak for those who cannot speak for themselves. In a world where powerful voices can overshadow the vulnerable, Yahweh reminds us of our responsibility to advocate for justice and the rights of the destitute. May we seek wisdom and courage to uphold...
reflection.zh: 呼吁国际外交以解决少数民族受压迫的问题，与圣经中为不能为自己说话之人发声的命令不谋而合。在一个强大声音可能掩盖弱势群体的世界里，雅伟提醒我们有责任倡导正义和维护贫困者的权利。愿我们寻求智慧和勇气，维护所有人的尊严，特别是那些声音被压制的人。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Taiwan says it was hit by ‘abnormal’ AI-assisted cyber-attack
title.zh: 台湾称遭受“异常”人工智能辅助网络攻击

summary.en: Taiwan reported detecting "abnormal" AI-assisted cyber-attacks on government agencies last month, originating from overseas. These attacks represent a new kind of threat, with suspected links to China-based hackers.
summary.zh: 台湾报告称，上个月侦测到来自海外、由人工智能辅助的“异常”网络攻击，目标是政府机构。这些攻击代表了一种新型威胁，据称与中国相关黑客有关。

body.en: Taiwan’s statement comes a day after reports that suspected China-linked hackers had carried out a first-of-a-kind breach Taiwan says it detected AI-assisted cyber-attacks on government agencies that came from overseas last month, a new kind of threat that has been reported as “first-of-a-kind breach”. The Ministry of Digital Affairs (MDA) said its cybersecurity monitoring units ‌detected the “abnormal attack” targeting government agencies, which began on 20 July. The National Institute of Cyber Security issued a series of warning alerts while it investigated. Continue reading...
body.zh: 台湾发表声明的前一天，有报道称疑似与中国有关的黑客实施了史无前例的违规行为。台湾表示，上个月检测到来自海外的针对政府机构的人工智能辅助网络攻击，这是一种新的威胁，被报道为“史无前例的违规行为”。数字事务部 (MDA) 表示，其网络安全监控单位检测到 7 月 20 日开始的针对政府机构的“异常攻击”。美国国家网络安全研究所在调查过程中发布了一系列警告。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The emergence of AI-assisted cyber-attacks highlights the constant need for vigilance in a rapidly changing world. Proverbs 27:12 reminds us that wisdom lies in foreseeing danger and taking appropriate refuge. As technology evolves, so must our discernment and protective measures, trusting Yahweh for guidance.
reflection.zh: 人工智能辅助的网络攻击的出现，凸显了在快速变化的世界中保持警惕的持续必要性。箴言27:12提醒我们，智慧在于预见危险并采取适当的避难措施。随着科技发展，我们的洞察力和保护措施也必须随之进步，信靠雅伟的指引。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: With Hollywood struggling in China, can the Odyssey draw a crowd?
title.zh: 好莱坞在中国市场举步维艰，《奥德赛》能否吸引观众？

summary.en: Christopher Nolan's summer blockbuster, "The Odyssey" (likely Oppenheimer), is set for release across China's Imax screens. This comes at a time when Western films generally face difficulties in the Chinese market, and the film itself has reportedly overcome significant opposition.
summary.zh: 克里斯托弗·诺兰的夏季大片《奥德赛》（很可能是《奥本海默》）将在中国各地的IMAX影院上映。目前西方电影在中国市场普遍举步维艰，而这部影片据报道也克服了来自世界首富的猛烈攻击。

body.en: Christopher Nolan’s epic will be released on Friday across most of the country’s 800 Imax screens, at a time when western films have been struggling The Odyssey, Christopher Nolan’s summer blockbuster juggernaut, has overcome an onslaught of attacks from the world’s richest man and stared down criticism from a classicist who translated the poem , to become one of the year’s most celebrated and highest-grossing films. But this week, the film faces one of its biggest challenges yet. Continue reading...
body.zh: 克里斯托弗·诺兰的这部史诗巨制将于周五在全国 800 块 Imax 银幕上上映，当时西方电影一直在苦苦挣扎，克里斯托弗·诺兰的夏季大片《奥德赛》克服了来自世界首富的猛烈攻击，也顶住了翻译这首诗的古典学家的批评，成为今年最著名和票房最高的电影之一。但本周，这部电影面临着迄今为止最大的挑战之一。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Launching any major endeavor, like a film in a challenging market, requires immense effort and hope for success. Proverbs 16:3 reminds us to commit our work to Yahweh, trusting that He will establish our plans. Even when facing significant headwinds, we can find peace in knowing that our diligent efforts are seen and can be blessed.
reflection.zh: 在充满挑战的市场中推出一部电影这样的大型项目，需要付出巨大的努力并寄予成功的希望。箴言16:3提醒我们，要将我们的工作交托给雅伟，相信他会成就我们的计划。即使面对重重阻力，我们也能在知道自己的辛勤努力被看见并蒙福时找到平安。

verse.textEn: Commit to Yahweh whatever you do, and he will establish your plans.
verse.textZh: 你所做的，要交托雅伟，你所谋的，就必成立。

title.en: Zhu Rongji obituary
title.zh: 朱镕基讣告

summary.en: Zhu Rongji, the fifth premier of the People’s Republic of China, has passed away at 97. He was widely recognized as an economic reformer who famously declared China 'the factory of the world' and was regarded as one of the country's most effective administrators.
summary.zh: 中华人民共和国第五任总理朱镕基逝世，享年97岁。他被广泛认为是经济改革家，曾宣布中国成为‘世界工厂’，并被视为该国最有效的管理者之一。

In 1991, Zhu was summoned to Beijing, in the footsteps of the then president and party secretary Jiang Zemin , and in the aftermath of the 1989 uprisings in Beijing and the collapse of the Soviet Union. His legacy reminds us that every life is a race run, with efforts and impacts that shape the world around us. Yahweh invites us to consider how we too might finish our own race with integrity and purpose.

title.en: The China factor in the United States' $500 million move in a tiny Australian town
title.zh: 美国在澳大利亚小镇投资5亿美元的“中国因素”

summary.en: The Pentagon is investing $500 million in a small Australian town in New South Wales, a move attributed to strategic considerations related to China. The reason for this sudden interest in a town of only 130 people is its role in broader international geopolitical dynamics.
summary.zh: 五角大楼正在澳大利亚新南威尔士州的一个小镇投资5亿美元，此举被认为是与中国相关的战略考量。这个只有130人的小镇突然受到关注，是因为它在全球地缘政治动态中的作用。

body.en:
The town of Fifield near Parkes is about a six-hour drive west of Sydney, and at the last Census was home to about 130 people. Now, the town has found itself at the centre of a major strategic play by the United States government.

The US Department of War has committed to make a conditional loan of US$400 million (about $566 million) to Sunrise Energy Metals, an Australian mining company hoping to deliver the world’s first supply of a key critical mineral outside of China.

Scandium is listed as a critical mineral in both Australia and the US, signalling its strategic importance in aerospace and defence.

This loan is another chapter in the US government’s search for secure critical mineral supply chains to reduce its dependency on Chinese supply. But success will require sustained investment and government support.

Scandium is a highly strategic metal used to produce ultra-high-strength alloys needed for the most advanced fighter jets. It is also used in solid oxide fuel cells, crucial for providing reliable power to artificial intelligence (AI) data centres.

First, demand for scandium is being driven by massive increases in defence spending across North America, Europe and Asia and an investment boom in power-hungry AI data centres.

Second, China’s sweeping export controls on rare earth elements, including scandium, have contributed to a persistent shortage of supply on the global market, pushing up prices.

These export controls are designed to maintain China’s dominance of supply chains for key critical minerals and slow down the US defence and industrial base.

Still, the market for scandium is tiny. According to statistics from the US Geological Survey, the entire world only consumed 60 tonnes of the metal in 2025.

Scandium is usually found in very small quantities. For that reason, until now, it has been exclusively produced as a byproduct of nickel and titanium processing.

This is what sets the Sunrise Energy Metals project apart — the proposed mine has scandium deposits in a high enough concentration to be the first primary source of scandium in the world.

If production goes ahead, and lives up to its promise of producing 60 tonnes of high-purity scandium each year by 2028, this would be enough to completely satisfy the current level of global demand.

According to the company, there is also potential to expand the project in the future and add another 120 tonnes of production.

The deal gives the US government first rights to purchase scandium from Sunrise Energy Metals, with production expected to start in late 2028.

body.zh: 帕克斯 (Parkes) 附近的菲尔菲尔德 (Fifield) 镇位于悉尼以西约 6 小时车程处，根据上次人口普查，该镇约有 130 人。现在，该镇已成为美国政府一项重大战略行动的中心。 美国陆军部已承诺向澳大利亚矿业公司 Sunrise Energy Metals 提供 4 亿美元（约合 5.66 亿美元）的有条件贷款，该公司希望在中国境外提供全球第一批关键矿物供应。 钪在澳大利亚和美国均被列为重要矿物，表明其在航空航天和国防领域的战略重要性。 这笔贷款是美国政府寻求安全的关键矿产供应链以减少对中国供应依赖的又一篇章。但成功需要持续的投资和政府支持。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 钪是一种高度战略性金属，用于生产最先进战斗机所需的超高强度合金。它还用于固体氧化物燃料电池，这对于为人工智能（AI）数据中心提供可靠的电力至关重要。 首先，北美、欧洲和亚洲国防支出的大幅增加以及耗电的人工智能数据中心的投资热潮推动了对钪的需求。 其次，中国对包括钪在内的稀土元素实行全面的出口管制，导致全球市场供应持续短缺，推高价格。 这些出口管制旨在维持中国在关键矿产供应链中的主导地位，并减缓美国国防和工业基础的发展。 尽管如此，钪的市场仍然很小。据美国地质调查局统计，2025年全球仅消耗了60吨金属。 钪的含量通常非常少。因此，到目前为止，它仅作为镍和钛加工的副产品生产。 这就是 Sunrise Energy Metals 项目的与众不同之处——拟建矿山的钪矿床浓度足够高，可以成为世界上第一个主要钪来源。 如果生产继续进行，并兑现到2028年每年生产60吨高纯钪的承诺，这将足以完全满足目前的全球需求水平。 该公司表示，未来还有可能扩大该项目，再增加120吨的产量。 该交易赋予美国政府从 Sunrise Energy Metals 购买钪的优先权，预计将于 2028 年底开始生产。 然而，这样做也存在一些风险……

title.en: Worldview 'gulf' behind strained Australia-China ties, former Australian ambassador says
title.zh: 前澳大利亚大使称，世界观“鸿沟”是澳中关系紧张的幕后原因

summary.en: Australia's former ambassador to China identified "diverging worldviews" as a key obstacle to fostering a robust relationship between the two nations.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚前驻华大使指出，“世界观差异”是澳中两国建立健康关系的主要障碍之一。

body.en:
Australia is unlikely ever to have a true partnership with China due to a mismatch of worldviews, rendering it pointless to pursue that goal, the nation's former top diplomat to China says.

But in an analysis piece for the Lowy Institute, Australia's former ambassador to China Graham Fletcher noted several wildcards, such as Chinese military action in Taiwan , could still disrupt the "modest new normal" of the relationship.

The change in government at the 2022 federal election acted as a circuit-breaker in increasingly fraught dealings between the nations, although they had still been marred by intimidatory military encounters involving Chinese forces, he said.

China sparked widespread international condemnation over its launch of a ballistic missile into the South Pacific in July following the signing of a landmark mutual defence alliance between Australia and Fiji.

The Albanese government sought to stabilise relations with China after diplomatic tensions peaked during the COVID-19 pandemic under then-prime minister Scott Morrison's leadership.

China slapped $20 billion in trade sanctions on Australian exports, measures that have slowly been wound back.

China is Australia's largest trading partner and is the destination for about a third of the nation's exports.

Fletcher said China had not given up hope of drawing Australia closer into its orbit, while Australia was more focused on consolidating its current relationship.

"But this relationship is unlikely ever to become genuinely close — like the relaxed, intimate fellowship Australia enjoys with like-minded partners elsewhere in its region and beyond," he said.

"The gulf in terms of diverging world views and national security agendas is simply too wide.

"It would be pointless for Canberra to pursue such a goal; it recognises this and is realistic."

The "mismatch" of world views made the relationship vulnerable to disruption, with key risks including another round of serious disagreements or the cataclysm of a conflict, including the use of force against Taiwan.

"An upheaval or conflict is always a possibility, though not in my opinion a strong one at present," the former diplomat said.

Australia would be on firmer ground when facing China if policies had cross-party support and politicians did not "seek to exploit difficulties for domestic advantage", Fletcher said.

"Bipartisanship produces policy consistency and limits China's ability to play games within the Australian system," he said.

Fletcher was Australia's ambassador to China from 2019 to 2023 and led the negotiating team in 2014 that helped seal a free trade agreement between the two...
body.zh: 澳大利亚前驻华最高外交官表示，由于世界观不匹配，澳大利亚不太可能与中国建立真正的伙伴关系，因此追求这一目标毫无意义。 但澳大利亚前驻华大使格雷厄姆·弗莱彻在洛伊研究所的一篇分析文章中指出，一些不确定因素，例如中国在台湾的军事行动，仍然可能破坏两国关系的“适度新常态”。 他说，2022 年联邦选举中的政府更迭为两国之间日益令人担忧的交易起到了断路器的作用，尽管它们仍然受到涉及中国军队的恐吓性军事冲突的损害。 在澳大利亚和斐济签署具有里程碑意义的共同防御联盟后，中国于 7 月向南太平洋发射弹道导弹，引发了国际社会的广泛谴责。 在时任总理斯科特·莫里森 (Scott Morrison) 的领导下，新冠肺炎 (COVID-19) 疫情期间外交紧张局势达到顶峰后，阿尔巴尼亚政府寻求稳定与中国的关系。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 中国对澳大利亚出口产品实施了价值 200 亿美元的贸易制裁，但这些措施已慢慢取消。 中国是澳大利亚最大的贸易伙伴，也是该国约三分之一出口的目的地。 弗莱彻表示，中国并未放弃将澳大利亚拉近其轨道的希望，而澳大利亚则更专注于巩固当前的关系。 “但这种关系不太可能变得真正亲密——就像澳大利亚与其地区及其他地方志同道合的伙伴所享有的轻松、亲密的友谊一样，”他说。 “世界观和国家安全议程的分歧实在太大了。 “堪培拉追求这样的目标是毫无意义的；它认识到这一点并且是现实的。” 世界观的“不匹配”使得两国关系容易受到破坏，其主要风险包括新一轮严重分歧或爆发冲突，包括对台湾使用武力。 这位前外交官表示：“动乱或冲突总是有可能发生，尽管我认为目前可能性不大。” 弗莱彻表示，如果政策得到跨党派支持，并且政客们不“寻求利用困难谋取国内利益”，那么澳大利亚在面对中国时将会更加坚定。 “两党合作带来了政策的一致性，并限制了中国在澳大利亚体系内玩弄游戏的能力，”他说。 弗莱彻于 2019 年至 2023 年担任澳大利亚驻中国大使，并于 2014 年领导谈判团队，帮助两国签署了自由贸易协定……

reflection.en: When nations face a "gulf" in worldviews, the path to peace can seem daunting. Yahweh's word encourages us to pursue peace actively, recognizing that while complete agreement may not always be possible, our commitment to peaceful coexistence remains vital. This calls for wisdom and perseverance in navigating complex international relations.
reflection.zh: 当国家之间面临“世界观鸿沟”时，通往和平的道路可能显得令人生畏。雅伟的话语鼓励我们积极寻求和平，认识到虽然完全一致可能并非总是可行，但我们对和平共处的承诺至关重要。这要求我们在复杂的国际关系中运用智慧和毅力。

title.en: More than one million evacuated, flights cancelled, as Typhoon Dolphin hits China
title.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击中国，逾百万人撤离，航班取消

summary.en: Typhoon Dolphin has led to the evacuation of over one million people and the cancellation of flights in China. The cyclone previously swept across Japan, causing injuries to six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.
summary.zh: 台风“海豚”袭击中国，导致逾百万人撤离，航班取消。此前，该气旋已横扫日本，造成六人受伤，并导致超过五万栋建筑断电。

body.en:
Typhoon Dolphin brought heavy rain to eastern China on Monday, causing hundreds of flight cancellations even as the storm weakened and some cities resumed public transport.

The typhoon had already swept across Japan’s southern Okinawa prefecture, injuring six people and cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings.

It then made landfall near Yuhuan in eastern Zhejiang province on Sunday evening, China's meteorological authorities said.

The storm packed maximum sustained winds of 151km/h near its centre at landfall, equivalent to a Category 1 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson scale.

Authorities had moved offshore workers to safety, ordered vessels back to port and increased checks at reservoirs, mountain streams, landslide-prone areas, construction sites and tourist locations.

The weather system lost power after making landfall, with China's National Meteorological Centre (NMC) issuing its least severe typhoon alert on Monday morning.

However, the NMC warned that parts of east and central China would continue to receive heavy rain for the next day.

The typhoon had triggered a top-level alert over the weekend, prompting over 1,000 flight cancellations and tens of thousands of evacuations.

Transport was widely disrupted across the east of the country, and more than one million people were evacuated from their homes.

Nine hundred and forty-three flights from Shanghai's two main passenger airports were cancelled, the airport authority said in an online post.

A 42-year-old tourist from Guangdong said he was stranded in Shanghai after his family's flight, scheduled to depart on Sunday, was cancelled due to Typhoon Dolphin.

He said the family had been rebooked on a flight at 10pm on Monday, although they were unsure whether it would be able to take off.

"To us Guangdong people, this typhoon is as ordinary as having a meal and feeling the wind. It's just part of everyday life," he said, adding that the storm did not appear particularly strong by the standards of China's southern coast.

In neighbouring Zhejiang province, the city of Wenzhou relocated more than 900,000 residents and opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters.

In Fujian province, authorities evacuated 98,900 people from high-risk areas after raising the typhoon emergency response to Level 3, according to Xinhua. Zhejiang, Shanghai and Jiangsu have also activated Level 3 emergency responses.

Fujian maritime authorities said 55 coastal passenger ferry routes had been suspended, all 115 offshore construction projects had been halted, and 290 construction vessels had been moved to sheltered waters.

body.en:
Ben Doherty Fri 14 Aug 2026 11.00 EDT Last modified on Fri 14 Aug 2026 11.02 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google War is Abbas’s* earliest memory.

As a child, the first iteration of Taliban rule forced his family to flee – with nothing but the clothes on their backs and what food they could carry – for the relative safety of far-distant hills.

War became his profession. Joining republican Afghanistan’s fledgling army, Abbas fought alongside American, Australian and British troops, believing in the foreigners’ ultimately false promise that they could bring peace and prosperity to his homeland.

Conflict is his constant attendant now, over Afghanistan’s border in neighbouring Iran, as the US, the country he fought with, rains bombs on the land of his exile. Back home, the resurgent Taliban – unreformed, unrepentant and firmly in charge – seek him still.

In the five years since Kabul dramatically fell back into the hands of the Taliban, those who served Afghanistan’s republican government have found themselves the targets of violent retribution. Those who took up arms against the Taliban are particular targets.

Abandoned US military databases – containing Afghans’ personal and biometric data such as fingerprints, photographs, and home addresses – are being used to hunt former soldiers who served the “infidel” west.

Social media groups share information of the latest atrocities, videos of former soldiers being whipped in the street, shot in summary executions, or dragged away in night raids to be tortured in Taliban prisons.

A bbas joined the military – initially at least – for the money. For a poor boy from the provinces, the army represented a regular income and a full belly, a reliable way to support his family. That there was a war on was barely a consideration: there was always a war on.

After basic training he passed a selection course to serve in the special forces.

“At first I joined for money but when I entered the commandos everything changed,” Abbas tells the Guardian. “There were foreign forces teaching us … they gave speeches about global terrorism.

“It was not about money any more. I became very committed, I just wanted to serve my country and fight Taliban and destroy the terrorist groups.”

He spent 12 years in the Afghan national army, most of those wearing the distinctive red badge of the special forces, “and we fought many hard battles”.

Abbas served alongside Australian troops in southern Afghanistan, night-time missions by helicopter in late 2011, in the restive and mountainous Khas Uruzgan district.

body.en: From Maga to Hungary’s Fidesz and Australia’s One Nation, politics is returning to its oldest question: what makes a life worth living? And liberalism needs a credible answer Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Those of us who live in liberal democracies carry an image of what a decent state should do. It should protect rights, grow the economy, maintain order, uphold fairness and arbitrate disputes. But on life’s deepest questions – what makes a life worth living, and what sort of person one ought to become – it is meant to show restraint. The state should not privilege one vision of human flourishing, let alone promote it. That is for individuals, families and communities to decide. To borrow the Minnesota governor Tim Walz’s golden rule of politics: “Mind your own damn business!” Consider birthrates . Across much of the wealthy world, they have fallen below replacement level. Fewer children mean fewer future workers, taxpayers and carers, and more pressure on pensions, health systems and aged care. Yet when liberal democracies encourage larger families, through baby bonuses or affordable childcare, they generally describe the goal as removing obstacles and expanding choice. Crucially, everyone should benefit: gay parents, straight parents, adoptive parents, biological parents, married parents, divorced parents – come one, come all. Continue reading...

summary.en: General practitioners are increasingly adopting a new practice during patient appointments, which is rapidly spreading. However, this new approach has not been universally accepted, with some expressing reservations.
summary.zh: 全科医生在病人就诊时正在迅速推广一项新做法。然而，并非所有人都对此信服。

body.en:
Walk into a GP's room these days, and you might be asked something new: "Do you consent to me using an AI transcription tool?"

It's a question that could soon become routine, with AI scribes now used by roughly 40 per cent of Australian GPs, up from 22 per cent in August 2024, according to survey data from the Royal Australian College of General Practitioners (RACGP).

Dr Janice Tan, a spokesperson for RACGP's expert committee, said GPs and clinicians use AI scribes to transcribe conversations with patients, take automated notes, and summarise what was discussed.

"During the consult, they [the AI scribe] listen and produce a draft note afterwards," she told SBS News. "Many also draft referral and specialist letters, care plans, and sometimes a plain-English summary for the patient."

But she's clear that the software documents interactions — it doesn't decide care plans.

"A product that starts suggesting a diagnosis or treatment the clinician didn't state is no longer a scribe, and sits in a different regulatory category," she said.

But another expert said more safeguards are needed to protect patients — and the benefits aren't as clear-cut as they first appear.

For GPs, Tan said the appeal comes down to reduced burnout and more patient-centred care.

"There's less documentation after hours, which is a real driver of burnout and people leaving the profession," she said.

"The doctor is looking at you rather than the keyboard … there's more patient-centred consults, not quicker ones."

"The most underused benefit is the patient-facing summary … [which features] what we discussed, what changed, when to come back. That's valuable for anyone managing something complex, and for carers."

She also said it allows for "better and more consistent records", which are particularly helpful if you don't always see the same GP.

Andrew Cullen from the University of Melbourne's School of Computing and Information Systems agrees GPs are the clear winners — but is more cautious about what patients get out of it.

"GPs and clinicians love scribes, because they no longer need to take notes — so they can devote more time to their patients," he told SBS News. "However, for patients, the benefit is a lot less clear."

His main concern is 'hallucination' — when AI systems, including scribes, confidently make up facts. He cited a 2025 study which he said found "up to 20 per cent of notes made by AI scribes contained major errors".

body.en:
When Ophelia Bryant first travelled to Italy in 1986, she says she felt something she could not quite explain.

Her parents had been born in Italy, as had all four of her grandparents. They immigrated to Australia in 1955, where Bryant was born three years later.

Italy has remained a constant in her life, with Bryant returning more than a dozen times to visit relatives and reconnect with her family roots.

But when she began looking into whether she could formally claim Italian citizenship, she discovered her family history came with a legal complication.

Her parents became Australian citizens in 1961, when Bryant was a child, and later formally renounced their Italian citizenship.

Under a restrictive interpretation of Italy's citizenship laws, known as the 'minor issue', that could break the line of citizenship transmission.

Now, a landmark decision by Italy's highest court has changed that legal interpretation — and Bryant is "optimistic because that door may finally be open".

The so-called minor issue arose from conflicting interpretations of Italy's 1912 citizenship law.

One provision established that children born overseas to an Italian citizen could acquire Italian citizenship from birth.

Another was interpreted as meaning that when an Italian parent became a citizen of another country, their minor children could lose their Italian citizenship along with them.

That interpretation gained ground through Italian court decisions from 2023 onwards, leading to the rejection of citizenship-by-descent applications.

But in July, Italy's Supreme Court's United Sections, the court's highest panel for resolving conflicting legal interpretations, ruled that citizenship acquired at birth was not automatically lost when an Italian parent subsequently naturalised in another country.

Brisbane-based Italian lawyer Fabrizio Fiorino, who advises clients on Italian citizenship applications, said the decision effectively restores the previous interpretation of the law.

"It was not a change in a provision, but it was a change in the interpretation of rules," he said.

He told SBS News the ruling means people who were Italian citizens from birth cannot simply be considered to have lost that citizenship because their parents later became foreign citizens while they were minors.

For thousands of people whose citizenship applications were rejected on that basis, the decision could provide a pathway back.

Italy's interior ministry has since issued a letter instructing authorities to follow the Supreme Court's interpretation.

United States President Donald Trump said he would consider granting an exemption to wide-ranging tariffs on Australian exports after a phone call with Prime Minister Anthony Albanese on Thursday.

Albanese said the conversation was "warm and productive", and that he had made the case for the US to drop its 12.5 per cent tariffs on Australia . Those new tariffs came into effect in July, replacing a previous 10 per cent tariff that was due to expire at the same time.

"I put the case as strongly as I could. It was a constructive discussion about why Australia should get at least the best treatment," he told reporters in Canberra on Friday.

"I did ask that Australia's position as a friend of the United States be considered, and the president agreed that he would give consideration to my request."

The US cited concerns over modern slavery laws when it announced wide-ranging tariffs on a range of countries earlier this year.

"I informed him about our record when it comes to dealing with issues such as modern slavery, the strengthening that we have put forward as well, to look and hold companies accountable for the supply-chain process as well," Albanese said.

"We have a different view, a different perspective. What I was able to do was to put the case to the president not in ideological terms, because the position is what it is."

The two leaders also discussed the AUKUS submarine deal between the two countries, the war in Iran, and Australia's recent alliances in the Pacific.

"We agreed [AUKUS] was a project that is and will continue to deliver benefits for the United States, for Australia, and for the United Kingdom," Albanese said.

The pair discussed the second pillar of the program, which includes enabling systems for uncrewed undersea vehicles.

The call came just hours after Pentagon official and former AUKUS sceptic Elbridge Colby confirmed to journalists that the mega deal was "full steam ahead".

Colby, who is the US undersecretary of war, originally wrote what was perceived as a sceptical review of the submarine deal before revising his writing to be more in line with Trump's view.

The Pentagon recently admitted construction of US Virginia-class nuclear submarines was languishing at about 1.1 to 1.2 boats per year, while 2.33 need to be made annually to meet AUKUS requirements.

Albanese said his phone call with Trump included an extensive update on the situation in the Middle East.

"We did continue to say that Iran shouldn't be allowed to have nuclear weapons. That represents a huge risk for the region," he said.

Australia's transport safety watchdog has launched an investigation into why it took four days for Sydney Airport to notify it of a third near-collision incident between two planes in as many weeks.

The incident happened on Sunday, just hours after a similar one which made national and international headlines , sparking widespread safety concerns after a crew member was injured.

The Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB) announced on Thursday night it had opened an investigation into the runway incursion, which involved two Boeing 737 jets at 10am on Sunday.

On Friday, ATSB chief commissioner Angus Mitchell said that "something has gone wrong" and that action needs to be taken to ensure similar incidents don't occur again.

"We want to understand why there was a delay in the reporting to us," he told the ABC.

The incident occurred when a Virgin Australia 737 was cleared by air traffic control (ATC) for take-off from Sydney’s runway 34L, the ATSB told SBS News in a statement.

"As the crew applied thrust for take-off, they observed a Qantas 737 crossing the runway ahead of them on taxiway Lima.

"Upon seeing the Qantas aircraft, the Virgin Australia crew reduced thrust and the aircraft came to a stop, roughly a kilometre from the intersection."

The Qantas jet crossed the Virgin flight's takeoff path, forcing ATC to cancel the latter's departure clearance "at the same time".

The ATSB said investigations were already underway, with evidence being gathered and interviews with the involved parties expected.

Earlier on Sunday, a Jetstar flight had to slam on the brakes to avoid hitting a Qatar Airways plane being towed across the tarmac.

The two weekend incidents come just weeks after two Qantas flights, with ATC permission, narrowly avoided contact in Sydney at the end of July.

All three incidents are under investigation by the national transport safety watchdog, which operates "no fault" fact-finding missions to prevent similar incidents from occurring, rather than to take punitive action.

title.en: A decade longer, $275,000 dearer: The trade-off facing Aussie home buyers
title.zh: 十年多了，贵了275,000澳元：澳大利亚购房者面临的权衡

summary.en: A new way into the housing market is gaining traction, but it comes with a hefty long-term cost.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Imagine paying a mortgage from today until 2066. For some Australians, that could become a reality as more lenders offer 40-year home loans.

In the last few years, an increasing number of smaller lenders in Australia have begun to offer these extended loan terms — a decade longer than the standard 30-year term.

Australian bank AMP was the latest to jump on the bandwagon, recently announcing a new 40-year mortgage product for investors.

It joins a relatively small list of competitors including Credit Union SA, Unity Bank, Great Southern Bank, RACQ Bank, Bank of Us, Liberty and Pepper Money.

Sally Tindall, data insights director at financial comparison site Canstar, told SBS News many of the 40-year mortgages are geared towards younger people and first-home buyers.

Last year, a Finder survey found that 30 per cent of Australians would take out a 40-year mortgage if it reduced their monthly repayments to a more affordable level.

But experts warn there are major downsides that would-be borrowers should weigh.

With house prices at historic highs, a longer loan term can make it easier for some Australians to enter the housing market by reducing monthly repayments, improving their serviceability or increasing how much they can borrow.

According to an analysis by Canstar, an additional decade of repayments on a $600,000 mortgage could reduce a borrower's initial monthly repayments by around $288 but result in nearly $275,000 in extra interest over the life of the loan.

"It improves someone's chances of getting the green light on a loan that they might not have otherwise been able to afford," Tindall told SBS News.

"But really, if you are someone that is struggling to pay off a debt over 30 years, it's worth stopping and thinking, well, is the size of the amount I want to borrow too high for my financial situation?"

Last year, when Great Southern Bank introduced a new 40-year loan, its chief customer officer, Rolf Stromsoe, suggested the product could be a stepping stone for first-home buyers, allowing them to enter the market before ultimately refinancing.

"As their needs evolve and their earnings capacity changes, they may refinance any number of times — but this is the loan that can start it all," he said.

But Tindall warned that refinancing may be a challenge with this type of product, given the limited pool of lenders that offer them and their high-risk profile.

It also exposes borrowers to the risk of being trapped in a loan they could struggle to refinance.

"Is that pay rise guaranteed? Is that promotion guaranteed? Absolutely not," Tindall asked.

reflection.en: This story draws attention to stewardship, provision, and the common good. 1 Peter 4:10 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with stewardship that serves neighbours, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到管家责任、供应与公共福祉。1 Peter 4:10提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以服事邻舍的好管家心态来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。
